chains.title: No TF-mediated effect: passenger intronic variant or linkage to a different causal variant
predictions: No allele-specific binding in EMSA or allele-specific ChIP at chr3:191441666 in HCT 116 or colon epithelium.
No allelic imbalance in MPRA/luciferase for the 200 bp window around the variant.
No colon eQTL for PYDC2, CCDC50 or PYDC2-AS1 appears with larger sample sizes; no genome-wide significant colorectal cancer association emerges.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-specific binding or reporter-activity difference between T and G is demonstrated.
Allelic base editing in colon cells or organoids changes expression of any neighbouring gene.
A colon eQTL or a credible colorectal cancer association for rs13078086 is reported.

chains.title: Loss of an intestinal homeobox (CDX2) site in the PYDC2-AS1 intron lowers PYDC2/PYDC2-AS1 expression

links.claim: The T allele is proposed to form an AT-rich CDX-family motif lost on T>G; within that homeobox specificity group CDX2 is picked as the intestine-restricted member. No motif scan, ChIP or QBiC-SELEX evidence was available for this site, so the binding claim and its direction are currently unsupported; coverage is not_checked.

The variant sits in a PYDC2-AS1 intron immediately beside a DNase-accessible enhancer-like cCRE, but it overlaps no cCRE or regulatory feature itself and sits at a non-conserved position (GERP -1.82).
PYDC2 is the closest protein-coding TSS (19.5 kb) and is in the cCRE's nearby-gene list, and the variant lies in its antisense transcript; this is proximity only, and no GTEx eQTL supports it.
Colon specificity is asserted from CDX2's known intestinal restriction; no cited data show CDX2 occupancy or element activity in HCT 116 or colon.
A PYDC2-inflammasome route to colorectal cancer is not supported by the literature search, whose hits concern other genes and cancers, and no GWAS or Open Targets signal exists.

predictions: A CDX/homeobox motif overlaps the variant in a PWM/QBiC scan, with T preferred.
Allelic imbalance in CDX2 ChIP favouring T, lost after CDX2 knockdown.
Base editing in colon organoids changes PYDC2/PYDC2-AS1 rather than CCDC50.
falsified_if: No CDX-family motif is affected by T>G.
CDX2 ChIP/CUT&RUN in colon cells shows no binding at the locus.
PYDC2 and PYDC2-AS1 expression are unchanged by allelic editing.

chains.title: Weakened CTCF binding beside the distal enhancer alters local insulation and CCDC50/PYDC2 expression
chains.element: Sequence 42 bp from EH38E2269392 (dELS), inside the PYDC2-AS1 intron

links.claim: CTCF was the only TF with any signal near this element (CTCF z 1.5 at EH38E2269392, a maximum over biosamples), but ENCODE ChIP-seq shows no CTCF peak containing the variant and none within 100 bp, so there is no evidence of CTCF occupancy here; the proposed stronger binding on T is unsupported and QBiC-SELEX coverage for CTCF was not checked.
The variant lies outside every cCRE; the nearest enhancer-like element (DNase z 3.5, H3K27ac z 1.8, biosample maxima only) is 42 bp away, so any boundary or looping role is speculative.
CCDC50 is listed as a nearby gene of EH38E2269392 and sits 112.6 kb downstream, but no eQTL links the variant to it in any GTEx tissue, including colon.
No biosample-specific data show this element is active in HCT 116 or colon; the DepMap context is given but untested here.
No GWAS Catalog or Open Targets evidence connects this variant to colorectal cancer, so any CCDC50-mediated risk effect is hypothetical.

predictions: A CTCF motif overlapping the variant would be scored by PWM/QBiC, with T preferred.
Allele-specific CTCF ChIP or CUT&RUN signal at this position in a colon line with the heterozygous genotype.
Allelic editing changes CCDC50 rather than PYDC2, and perturbs a local loop detectable by 4C/Hi-C.
falsified_if: No CTCF motif overlaps chr3:191441666 in a PWM/QBiC scan.
CUT&RUN or deeper CTCF ChIP in colon cells shows no occupancy at this site (E08 already argues against it).
CRISPR deletion of the adjacent element leaves CCDC50 unchanged.

chains.title: Alt allele creates a TCF7L2 (Wnt effector) site feeding the adjacent enhancer

links.claim: TCF7L2 was chosen within the TCF/LEF specificity group as the dominant colorectal family member, but this rests on prior knowledge only: ENCODE shows no TCF7L2 peak containing the variant and none within 100 bp, and no motif scan or QBiC model was consulted.
The nearest enhancer-like cCRE is 42 bp away with accessibility and H3K27ac in some biosample; the variant itself is in no cCRE.
CCDC50 appears only as a nearby-gene annotation of that cCRE at 112.6 kb; PYDC2 is closer (19.5 kb) and no eQTL distinguishes them.
No cited evidence demonstrates Wnt-dependent activity of this element in HCT 116; the Wnt context is assumed from the cell line's known biology.
No GWAS or Open Targets association supports a colorectal cancer effect.

predictions: A TCF/LEF motif is created by T>G in a motif scan.
Reporter activity higher for G specifically in Wnt-active colorectal lines, abolished by beta-catenin or TCF7L2 knockdown.
Allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy favouring G in a deeper or different colorectal TCF7L2 experiment.
falsified_if: No TCF/LEF motif is created by T>G.
No allelic difference, or T stronger, in colorectal reporter assays.
TCF7L2 occupancy remains absent in colorectal lines (E09 already argues against it).

grades_v0.reason: E03 gives only a max-over-biosamples CTCF z 1.5 for a cCRE 42 bp away. It does not show CTCF at the variant, a motif, or an allele effect. The 'T binds more' direction is unsupported, and no QBiC or chip_peaks lookup was done.
The cCRE (DNase z 3.5, H3K27ac z 1.8) is real but does not overlap the variant, and biosample-specific values are absent. A boundary or looping role is speculative.
E03 lists CCDC50 as a nearby gene and E02 gives the distance, but no eQTL, Hi-C or CRISPR data link the element to CCDC50. PYDC2 is closer, and CTCF insulation could affect several genes.
No evidence IDs are cited. Nothing shows the element is active in HCT 116 or colon, and E03 gives only biosample maxima.
E04 and E05 show no association. The claim is acknowledged to lack evidence, and E06 does not address CCDC50.
E01 is only a VEP consequence and says nothing about TCF motifs or binding. TCF7L2 is chosen by prior knowledge, not by the evidence, and no motif scan or ChIP is cited.
The adjacent cCRE has accessibility and H3K27ac, but the variant is outside it. A Wnt-responsive role is inferred and not shown.
CCDC50 is only a nearby-gene annotation. 'Nearest protein-coding gene' is also wrong for the claim: PYDC2 is closer, and CCDC50 is 112.6 kb away.
E06 is a PYDC2/colorectal cancer search whose hits are irrelevant to Wnt activity in HCT 116. It does not support the claim.
E04 and E05 show no association, and the chain concedes this.
E01 says nothing about a CDX motif. The AT-rich motif is speculative and generic, and CDX2 is selected by expression logic without any lookup.
The intronic position in PYDC2-AS1 is shown by E01 and the neighboring cCRE by E03. The variant is not in the cCRE, and no CDX2 binding is shown there.
PYDC2 is the nearest gene (E02) and is in the cCRE's nearby list (E03), but this is proximity only. The ASO transcript and PYDC2 have no eQTL or perturbation support.
No evidence is cited for CDX2 or for colon-specific activity. HCT 116 CDX2 expression is asserted and not checked.
E06 contains no PYDC2 colorectal inflammasome evidence. The listed hits concern other genes or cancers, so the inflammasome route is unsupported.
E01 gives no NF-kB motif or binding data. NFKB1 is picked from a group without a reason beyond expression, and no QBiC, ChIP or expression data are cited.
E03 confirms no cCRE overlap and E01 gives GERP -1.82, which fits a non-functional site. This is a weak, negative-context argument and is not proof.
E02 gives PYDC2 as the nearest gene, and E05 shows no Open Targets record. No eQTL was checked, so absence of a link is not shown.
E06 is irrelevant to NF-kB activity in colonic mucosa.
E04 and E05 show no signal, consistent with no phenotype, but a null result is not evidence against an effect.

grades_final.reason: E08 shows no CTCF ChIP-seq peak containing the variant or within 100 bp, and E03 only gives a biosample-maximum CTCF z 1.5 at a cCRE 42 bp away. Nothing shows CTCF binds here, and no QBiC or motif evidence supports T binding more. Coverage is not_checked; a qbic_tf_detail lookup for CTCF would be the check.
E03 shows the variant is in no cCRE, with the nearest dELS 42 bp away. This is epigenomic context only and shows no boundary or insulator role for the variant site.
CCDC50 is only a nearby-gene annotation of the cCRE (E03) and is 112.6 kb away (E02). E07 shows no eQTL, and no perturbation or looping data link the variant to CCDC50 over PYDC2.
E03 gives only maxima across biosamples, with nothing specific to HCT 116 or colon. The cell type is merely the given context.
E04 and E05 show no GWAS or Open Targets association with colorectal cancer, and nothing links CCDC50 to the phenotype.

E09 shows no TCF7L2 peak containing the variant or within 100 bp. TCF7L2 was chosen from the TCF/LEF group by prior knowledge, and no motif scan or QBiC evidence supports alt-allele gain. Coverage is not_checked; a qbic_tf_detail lookup for TCF7L2 would be the check.
E03 shows an enhancer-like cCRE 42 bp away, but the variant is outside every cCRE. The evidence is proximity and context only.
CCDC50 appears only as a nearby-gene annotation (E03) at 112.6 kb, while PYDC2 is closer (E02). E07 shows no eQTL, so there is no evidence to choose CCDC50.
No evidence is cited, and Wnt-dependent activity in HCT 116 is assumed from prior knowledge.
E04 and E05 show no association supporting a colorectal cancer effect.

No evidence is cited. There is no motif scan, ChIP or QBiC data, and CDX2 was picked from a homeobox group by prior knowledge with direction unsupported. Coverage is not_checked; a qbic_tf_detail lookup for CDX2 would be the check.
E01 and E03 place the variant in a PYDC2-AS1 intron next to an accessible dELS, but it overlaps no cCRE or regulatory feature and the site is non-conserved (GERP -1.82). The evidence is context only.
PYDC2 is the closest protein-coding TSS (E02), is listed near the cCRE (E03), and the variant lies in its antisense transcript (E01). This is proximity only, and E07 shows no eQTL.
No evidence is cited. Colon specificity is asserted from CDX2's known restriction, with no data on CDX2 occupancy or element activity in HCT 116 or colon.
E06 hits concern other genes and cancers and do not support PYDC2 in colorectal cancer. E04 and E05 show no association.

checks.why: Tests whether a CTCF ChIP peak contains the variant in HCT 116, the only TF with any signal near the element.
A colon eQTL for CCDC50, PYDC2 or another gene would discriminate target genes and against H0.
Tests for TCF7L2 occupancy at the variant in a Wnt-active colorectal line, and can falsify H2 directly.

next_experiment: Run a QBiC-SELEX / PWM scan of the 25 bp window around chr3:191441666 for all TF models. It is the cheapest test that separates the top two chains: the null predicts no meaningful predicted binding change for a colon-expressed TF, while H3 requires a CDX/homeobox site with the T allele preferred (and would also check the CTCF and TCF/LEF options already undercut by E08 and E09).
